text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The ruling Homeland Union party on Saturday named its leader Vytautas Landsbergis as its candidate to run in the Decemeber presidential election.
- The new official residence of Lithuania's president in the centre of Vilnius will be opened on Friday, May 16.

- Twenty-three foreign law firms and investment banks expressed their interest to become a lead advisor to the Lithuanian government on the privatisation of Lithuanian Telecom. The advisor is expected to be chosen by the end of June.
- The Lithuanian government intends to sell its 30 percent stake in Baltijos Shipyard on the Vilnius bourse in June.
- Uzbekistan owes Lithuanian companies around 40 million litas.
- Vytautas Landsbergis said he sees President Algirdas Brazauskas as his main competitor in December's presidential race.
- Lithuania wants to establish a no-visa regime with Switzerland.
- Mobil Sales and Supply corporation might sue Lietuvos Energija for failing to pay for the heating oil supplied in 1995.
- Klaipeda Transport Fleet said it earned 11 million litas in the first quarter of 1997 compared to 5.5 million litas in the same period in 1996.
- Snaige fridge producer plans to boost its share capital to 60 million litas from 40 million litas.
